body.statement:
Suppose either that the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\mathrm{oeq:effective\mbox{-}compatible\mbox{-}density}\) is available, or that a separately proved sufficient compatibility package supplies the same computable finite-library modulus and certified coverage, separated-risk, and ledger inequalities.  Then, for every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\operatorname{CertGluePFL}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\) terminates and returns a replayable globally honest primal rule, a finite rational atomic dual, outward rational endpoints
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\leq\varepsilon,
\]
and explicit total recursive bounds \(N_{\mathrm{glue}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{cut}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), and \(\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), recorded in \(\mathsf C\).  The theorem is conditional and does not resolve the open-ended compatibility-density question.
body.justification: A convergence theorem without a finite stopping recurrence would not support certified statistical practice.
body.gap: Jones and Peet give an a priori integration error, Jungen, Djelassi, and Mitsos give conditional convergence for finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs, and Cousins and Vempala give randomized Gaussian-volume approximation; none certifies this function-valued minimax game with exact honesty and a matched atomic dual.
body.consumer: For the Job Corps assertion list, the output archives the exact observed-cell-to-\(\mathfrak G_0\) encoding, the simultaneous honest label rule, the primal and atomic-dual objects, and every outward integration and repair charge; this replayable certificate is required because a floating-point optimizer cannot establish global honesty on tied capacity, sign, or cross-quantile faces.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: conditional effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}
Assume the conditional premise in the statement; it is not derived here.  Precisely, the premise supplies a computable sequence \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) and finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) such that, for every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\),
\[
 c\{Q_j(K)\}\geq1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),
 \tag{36}
\]
\[
 r\{Q_j(K)\}\leq R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
 \tag{37}
\]
Here \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of all semantic coverage probabilities and \(r(Q)\) is the separated diameter risk.  The finite record also certifies the canonical-section, positive-weight safety, simultaneous-collar, translated-tail, and refinement-count facts needed for (36)--(37).  No refinement-independent ledger constant is used.

At stage \(s\), enumerate all library indices \(j\leq s\), all records in \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of code length at most \(s\), all rational incidence forests and semantic projections in those records, and the first \(s\) rational choices of integration and rounding precision.  The weighted ledger gives outward rational enclosures
\[
 c^-_{Q,s}\leq c(Q),
 \qquad r(Q)\leq r^+_{Q,s}.
 \tag{38}
\]
Accept a record only after every rational polyhedral incidence, protected-neighborhood, Gaussian-tail, covariance, quadrature, and rounding check supporting (38) has passed.  Thus acceptance uses no uncertified floating-point sign.

Intersect \(c^-_{Q,s}\) with \([0,1]\), and define
\[
 \rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
 \qquad q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
 \tag{39}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
 0\leq\rho_{Q,s}\leq1-\eta<1,
 \qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0,
 \tag{40}
\]
so the division is valid.  Equations (38)--(39) imply \(c(Q)\geq1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  The exact-repair lemma makes \(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) globally honest and gives
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 \leq R_r(Q^+)
 \leq r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.
 \tag{41}
\]
Outward rational interval arithmetic produces a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last expression.

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic duals in \(\mathrm{thm:attainment\mbox{-}atomic\mbox{-}duality}\).  Their rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points admit exact membership checks in each finite union \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\): membership and polyhedral Mahalanobis distance reduce to finitely many polynomial sign and active-set checks.  Refine the Gaussian integrations for a feasible dual \(\nu\) until a rational lower enclosure \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) is available.  Every such number is a valid lower certificate.  Put
\[
 L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},
 \qquad
 U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s}.
 \tag{42}
\]
Whenever both endpoints exist, weak duality and (41) give
\[
 L_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\leq U_s.
 \tag{43}
\]

Every fixed stage terminates.  Its enumerated collections are finite, rational polyhedral feasibility and incidence are finite rational linear programs, and Gaussian integration is enclosed on a rational box by interval subdivision.  On the box, each accepted record carries a certified modulus; off the box, the recorded Gaussian tail tends effectively to zero.  Hence every requested positive enclosure width is reached after finitely many subdivisions.

Let \(K^*\) be the attaining honest rule supplied by atomic duality, so
\[
 R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{44}
\]
For rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine outward evaluation of the record supplied by (36)--(37) gives
\[
 c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\geq c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
 \qquad
 r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.
 \tag{45}
\]
Thus \(\rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\leq\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\), and (37), (41), and one more outward width \(\zeta\) imply
\[
 U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 +D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
 +\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
 {\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
 \tag{46}
\]
The right side approaches the minimax value by first increasing \(j\) and then decreasing \(\zeta\).  Atomic duality also supplies enumerated finite lower certificates converging upward to that value.  Therefore
\[
 L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),
 \qquad \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\leq M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{47}
\]
Together with (43), this proves that some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\).

For the explicit cost receipt, let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) count operations of type \(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\) at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest integer bit length occurring there.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
 C_i(0)=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),\qquad
 C_i(s+1)=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),
 \tag{48}
\]
\[
 B(0)=b(\mathfrak G,0),\qquad
 B(s+1)=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
 \tag{49}
\]
Let
\[
 s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=
 \min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\leq\varepsilon\}.
 \tag{50}
\]
The test is rational and (47) proves its search halts.  Hence \(s_*\) is total recursive under the conditional premise.  Set
\[
 N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
 \tag{51}
\]
Archive at stage \(s_*\) the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum and the finite atomic dual attaining the finite maximum in (42).  Equations (43), (50), and (51) give the endpoints, gap, termination, replayability, and five-part receipt.  The only use of compatibility density was the expressly conditional input (36)--(37); the proof does not answer the OEQ.
